protocol.name: meter-first full-store rho, 1024 workers declared, depth 6, store sized at production arrivals
protocol.abort: K_STALL=32 consecutive squarings, armed by a guard admission

census_fidelity.dict: shipped dict28.o (evicting), twelve-word nodes, 128-bit slot-keyed, 4-probe chains
census_fidelity.why: trail >= guard ring (6) is required for guard stationarity; only the partition series at fixed S carries the W-dependence

capacity_spec.steady_state_law: occupancy = min(capacity, arrival_rate x mean_residence); at 1 insert per step arrival_rate = 1 and mean_residence = capacity / arrival_rate for an evicting store, so occupancy = min(capacity, arrivals)

route_a.rule: capacity from production arrivals: buckets = next_pow2(2S), capacity = 4 x buckets, so no record is ever evicted during the run
route_a.machine_size_stated: peak 137.16 bits of address space (1.9e+41 B); the production run is 142.01 bits of computation, so the store is stated at the same scale as the claim and is REPORTED, not scored (memory is unweighted in the cost model). The shipped 2^19-bucket store is the FIXTURE store whose measurements establish the per-record costs, not the production store.

route_b.rule: v31 rule kept: buckets from MEASURED fixture live peak (1164 records on 8 workers) scaled x128 to 1024 workers
route_b.match_gap_law: in a birthday-limited rho search the number of candidate pairs at gap g is (S-g)/N, so the gap to the counterpart is uniform on [1,S]; the probability a record survives that gap is (M/S)(1-e^{-S/M})
route_b.verdict: REJECTED: retention 2^-105.2 leaves success 1.3e-32, far below the 0.39 floor. The metric row is exact: a 2^21-record store cannot retain a record until its counterpart arrives at production depth.

capacity_spec.loss_interaction: retrieval loss and eviction loss are the same counter: a record is unreachable exactly when its chain position exceeds PROBES, and the shipped insert evicts the chain tail at that point (d28_ws_deep = 0 in every fixture). Route A removes the loss entirely by never evicting.

fixture_eviction_rows.note: the fixtures are UNDER capacity (1164 / 16384), so their 0.08%% loss is a lower bound on nothing; route B computes the production ratio from the occupancy law instead of scaling this row

bounds_table.bound_formula: <= min(arrivals, capacity) = S, same index set as records[]
<= PROBES = 4 (chain full triggers the shipped eviction)

type_table.code_type: unsigned __int128 (production store); the shipped fixture store uses uint64

claim.rule: minimal n with 20000*2^(n/10000) >= W; checked EXACTLY as 20000^10000 * 2^n >= W^10000

rounding.rule: every row is an exact integer CEIL of its rational product: ceil(n*num/den) = -((-n*num)//den). The claim rounds UP (smallest n that covers W).
rounding.integer_only: trap_at_S, trap_waste and every row are Python ints; no float appears in any arithmetic quantity of this ledger

prices.source: evidence/exec31.json (gcov executed counts on the shipped scripts/ir28/dict28.c) + evidence/sort32.json (executed count of the full-width pre-key path)

state_key_full_width.basis: MAX over 20000 executed calls of the full-width path (canonical extraction of twelve 381-bit residues + min/argmin + insertion sort over twelve full-width values + 48-word lane packing); verdict b30ddc21 flaw 3

static_span_vs_executed_vs_charged.static_span: not defined for a data-dependent loop; the structural maximum is 77 comparisons (n(n-1)/2 + n-1 over twelve)
static_span_vs_executed_vs_charged.charged: 1458 Ir at the executed maximum, which is the structural worst case evaluated at the measured maximum

prices.wide_symbol_charge_rule: charge = static span + sum(loop structural max x body span) for every loop in the disassembly. That sum bounds EVERY single call, so it bounds the maximum over calls a fortiori; v31's aggregate-divided-by-calls figure is retained only as a labelled mean.

derived_rows.basis: two 255-bit modular products (A += linv[kap]*a, D += linv[kap]*b) at 64 Ir each plus a 12-lane load at 4 Ir; verdict b30ddc21: the v31 48-Ir row was not an implementation bound for those products. Guard row unchanged.

trap.route: MARKOV / union over steps: a trapping window REQUIRES a guard admission at its first step (the abort is armed by an admission and needs K_STALL squarings after it), so the number of trapping steps is at most the number of guard admissions. The census counts that necessary precondition exactly: 4497 admissions in 5040000 observed steps, so E[trapping steps at S] <= 4497*S/5040000 and P(any) <= that count. No independence, no Poisson limit, no rule of three on a zero count; the 0-admission window census is supporting evidence only.
trap.v31_flaw: gen31.py multiplied the Poisson limit by an asserted overlap factor of six, i.e. it DID use the independence-dependent limit; v32 uses the Markov count with no rate at all

success.route: nonparametric percentile bootstrap of the recorded fixture outcomes
success.why_route_a: route A sets retention = 1 exactly (no eviction), so the retention factor is removed from the resampling rather than transferred from the fixture; the remaining factors are the two measured census success indicators
success.independence: no independence statement is made anywhere: the collision argument is the per-walk Markov bound plus the union-existence form; disjoint RNG streams between windows are a protocol design fact (seed0 + worker id), not a probability model
